questions.text: How does a sparsely routed Mixture-of-Experts layer increase model capacity without running every expert for every token?

options.A: It removes unused experts permanently after processing the first token.
options.B: It stores only one expert’s weights and recreates all others from the input.
options.C: It replaces all attention and feed-forward computation with a lookup table.
options.D: It stores multiple experts but routes each token through a selected subset.

questions.explanation: MoE stores many experts while activating only a subset for each token, separating total expert capacity from per-token expert computation.

questions.text: A toy MoE has 8 equal-sized routed experts and selects 2 per token, with no shared experts. Ignoring the router and all other layers, what fraction of expert parameters is active per token?
questions.explanation: Two of eight equal-sized experts are active, giving 2/8 = 1/4 of the expert parameters.

questions.text:
Which experts are selected, and what scores are used to compute their gate weights?

```python
scores = [3.0, 2.0, 1.0]
bias = [-3.0, 0.0, 2.0]
biased = [s + b for s, b in zip(scores, bias)]
top_idx = sorted(range(3), key=lambda i: -biased[i])[:2]
chosen = [scores[i] for i in top_idx]
# gates = softmax(chosen)
```
questions.explanation: Biased scores [0,2,3] select experts 2 then 1. Gating uses their original scores [1,2], not their biased selection scores.
